summary: Dörte Kamarid works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, with Helmut Tauscher serving as her MA supervisor.

E. D. Hirsch, a scholar in philosophy and other fields, studied at Metairie Park Country Day School and Cornell University (~1946–1950). He held posts at Wesleyan University (~1956–1957) and the University of Virginia (~1966).

E. F. Schumacher worked in philosophy and other fields, studying at the University of Bonn, New College, Columbia University, and LSE, under Edward Conze. He held academic posts at Columbia University (~1931–1933) and the University of Oxford (~1942–1944).

Tibetologist E. Gene Smith studied under Turrell V. Wylie and several Tibetan masters. He served at the Library of Congress (1968–1985, 1994–1997) and founded and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (1999–2010).

E. W. Adikaram was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Wesley College, the University of Colombo, SOAS, and the University of London under William Stede, later serving as principal of Ananda Sastralaya in 1934.

Eberhard Fischer specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. After earning his PhD from the University of Basel (~1960–1965), he served as director of the Museum Rietberg (1972–1998) and president of the Rietberg Society (~1972–2001).

Eberhard Sandschneider, a sinologist, earned his PhD at Saarland University (~1981–1986). He served as professor at Mainz (1995–1998), professor and director at the Free University of Berlin (from 1998), and director at the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Eberhard Schrader worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen (~1854–1858), he held posts at Zurich (~1863–1870), Giessen (~1870–1873), Jena (~1873–1875), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1875–1908).

Edeltraud Harzer works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Charles University and the University of Washington, with traditional training under Shree Narayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya, she held posts at Washington, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas at Austin.

Edgar Howard Sturtevant was a linguist working in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Illinois College and Indiana University Bloomington, he held academic posts at Columbia University (~1908–1920) and Yale University (~1923–1943).
Edgar Polomé was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Université catholique de Louvain (~1938–1949). He later served on the faculty at the University of Texas at Austin (~1961–1990).

Edith Wyschogrod worked in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Hunter College (~1947–1951) and Columbia University (~1965–1970), and was the J. Newton Rayzor Professor of Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (1992–2002).
Edmond Yee works in religious studies and sinology. He served on the faculty at both the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union from ~1986 to 2008.

Edmund Hardy was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. After studying under Kuno Fischer at Heidelberg, he served as a professor of philosophy at Freiburg (1885–1893) and held a chair at Fribourg (1894–1898).
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist. He graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886 and pursued studies under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edmund Ronald Leach studied at Clare College, Cambridge, and the LSE. He held positions at the LSE (~1947–1953) and the University of Cambridge (1953–1978), where he was also provost of King's College (1966–1979).

Edo Shonin works in religious studies and related fields. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and as Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Böhmer was a linguist who studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1847–1851). He held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (~1872–1892).

Sinologist Eduard Erkes studied at the University of Leipzig under August Conrady (~1908–1913), whom he later succeeded. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (~1917–1958) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1947–1958).

Linguist and Indologist Eduard Hermann earned his PhD under Berthold Delbrück at Jena (~1891–1893). He held posts at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and served as professor at the University of Göttingen (1917–1937).
